actual_chain: StorageBlockEntity loads owned wrapper; wrapper restores category settings and slot counts. LimitedBarrel loadAdditional calls setFixedSettings on no-level/server context.
onLoad non-linked owner makes memory matching NBT-sensitive, reinforces display/no-sort slots and refreshes item display.
setFixedSettings compares each selected collection size with slot count. NoSort selectSlots unions 0..N into existing selected set and serializes through category save callback.
SettingsHandler registration callbacks persist category and mark owner dirty; StorageSettingsHandler stores category children in owned settings compound.
StorageContainerMenuBase client sort sends action; server action dispatch reaches wrapper.sort. Wrapper unions category exclusions and partition exclusions; linked wrapper delegates.

InventorySorter compacts only non-skipped slots, removes skipped slots from memorized work, and leaves skipped slots untouched while writing others. InventoryHelper compaction confirms exclusions before stack merging.

InventoryHandler forwards partition no-sort set. Partitioner absent baseIndexes defaults one default part; interface default no-sort returns empty. No unconditional extra default-part protection is inferred.
findings: Cardinality is not exact slot membership: N=4 selected {1,2,3,7} bypasses no-sort reconstruction while missing slot0. This is a static policy counterexample, not a native exploit reproduction.
Starting {7} with N=4 unions to {0,1,2,3,7}; size remains wrong on later loads. Repair does not remove stale indices.

Display list raw deserialization allows duplicates/out-of-range entries; selectSlots appends and returns early at itemNumberLimit before serialization/full render update. This is support for the same fixed-policy mechanism, zero separate credit.
onLoad checks !isLinkedStorage but loadAdditional does not; ownership guard asymmetry observed, no cross-owner runtime claim.
Other partition exclusions, accessibility and memory filters can mask the observed policy hole; no universal actual item loss/reorder claim.

semantic_dedup.difference: Existing stack Size/Slot bounds decoder; current mechanism is serialized behavioral slot policy reconstructed for a concrete limited-barrel owner and consumed by sorting.
Existing missing-layout default partition restore; current category-level per-compartment exclusion survives into sorting; partition helper is support only.
Existing item/stack memory filter decoder; NBT-sensitive memory activation is support, not new credit.
Existing canonical owner/cache invalidation; wrapper restoration is supporting entry only, not recounted.

application_to_dynasty: When later gate permits migration changes, validate exact finite slot/key membership against current owner schema, not collection cardinality, and preserve serialized content separately from derived behavior. Do not put world/container settings into player Clone whitelist or mint quest rewards during migration.
